header.title: From tokens to numbers
header.intro: Follow one real token from its ID label to the numbers a model can use.

actions.seeNext: See how the row is used

notice.default: We’ve loaded a verified example. You can replace it anytime.
notice.transient: These are your latest token cards from Split text.

real.title: Choose one real token
real.instruction: Click a token and watch its real Qwen ID badge appear.
real.labelTitle: An ID is only a lookup label.
real.labelMeaning: It helps the model find the correct record. It is not a score and does not contain the token’s meaning.

lookup.title: What is the ID for?
lookup.intro: The ID tells the model where to look in its learned table.
lookup.label: ID label {{id}}
lookup.picture: This is a picture to explain the lookup idea—not a literal drawer inside the model.
lookup.truth: The ID chooses a row. Its digits do not turn into the values inside that row.
lookup.discovery: ID {{id}} selects row {{id}} from the real model table.

training.title: Where did the row come from?
training.intro: The values were learned before you opened this lab.
training.flowLabel: Training examples adjust a learned number table
training.notCalculatedTitle: ID {{id}} does not calculate the row.
training.notCalculatedBody: Training learned the row’s values. The ID only retrieves the matching row.

realRow.title: Why can’t we show Qwen’s real row?
realRow.intro: Qwen row {{id}} exists, but it is part of the full model.
realRow.weights: The learned row is stored in Qwen’s model weights.
realRow.tokenizerOnly: This browser loaded the tokenizer, not Qwen’s model weights.
realRow.teachingBody: It shows the shape of the idea without pretending to be Qwen data.

toy.label: Made-up teaching values — not Qwen values
toy.title: Inspect one tiny teaching row
toy.intro: Open one anonymous example row and watch its three values appear together.
toy.waiting: First use the real ID and continue through the truthfulness break.
toy.closed: Open this row to reveal its three made-up values.

revealSteps.first: One position appears. It has no simple meaning by itself.
revealSteps.second: Another position joins it. The values are meant to work together.
revealSteps.complete: All three values form one teaching row. A real model row is much longer.

toy.wholeRowTitle: Treat the whole row as one starting representation.
toy.wholeRowBody: Later model calculations can transform and combine this row with the rows for surrounding tokens.
toy.noSingleMeaning: No single value simply means “verb”, “important”, or “learn”. Positive is not good and negative is not bad.

nextUse.title: What does the model do with the row?
nextUse.intro: The ID and the row have different jobs.
nextUse.idJob: Useful for finding the matching row.
nextUse.idLimit: It is one arbitrary label—not useful calculation material by itself.
nextUse.rowJob: A starting numerical representation that later calculations can transform and combine.
nextUse.rowTruth: The three shown values are still only a teaching example.
nextUse.contextChanges: Surrounding token rows affect one another during later processing.
nextUse.conceptOnly: Concept only — no Qwen probabilities are being generated.
nextUse.discovery: The model processes the token rows together. Later calculations give possible next tokens different chances.

summary.title: The complete journey
summary.id: The tokenizer gives a token an ID label.
summary.row: The ID selects one learned row in the model’s table.
summary.training: Training learned the row values—the ID did not calculate them.
summary.context: Later calculations combine token rows and context to work out what may come next.
summary.next: Next, explore how surrounding words change the model’s working representations.

technical.title: Learn the technical words
technical.intro: The default pictures use plain language. These are the precise technical names.

tokenId.definition: An integer that indexes one token in the tokenizer vocabulary and selects the matching model row.

vector.definition: A learned parameter row used as the token’s initial numerical representation.

matrix.definition: The learned table containing one parameter row for each vocabulary entry.

weights.definition: The numerical parameters learned during training, including the embedding table.

training.definition: Values repeatedly adjusted while the model learns patterns from training examples.

dimensions.definition: Positions in a vector. A single dimension normally has no simple, stable human-readable meaning.

technical.truth: This lab loads the real Qwen tokenizer only. It does not load or fabricate Qwen embeddings, model calculations, or probabilities.
